agent_priors_used: Agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): repeatedly repairing the same measurement instrument on the same gate is a local attractor and typically has decaying marginal value; after a bounded number of control-plane defects the right move is to repair the shared certificate/attainability machinery once rather than keep editing one predicate.

Agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): already-frozen or executed experiments should be allowed to resolve before strategic redirection, because superseding them discards invested evidence and confounds inference.

Agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a claim's registry status can be staler than its accepted running state; the effective status carried in the Codex claim state should govern, and local registry fields should not override it.

Agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): oracle/instrument scope bounds (trained-and-test on one authored surface versus arbitrary transitions) are a classic generalization gap; testing the same detector against changes induced outside its author's surface is the correct next discriminating step.

Agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a treatment arm must be shown to have dynamic range against its comparator before an expensive multi-arm benchmark is meaningful; a 1.0-success comparator ceiling yields a non-identifying test.

Agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): acquisition-cost structure is a first-class research question for crawling agents; if structured discovery channels collapse depth cost, then traversal-path persistence is the wrong memory abstraction.

Agent prior (NOT SPIDER evidence): a falsifier that is arithmetically checkable and satisfiable in BOTH directions, with an attainability certificate, materially reduces empty-accept-region and unsatisfiable-predicate failures.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Compared with (a) the maintenance/invalidation alternative (how the cost of keeping a persisted path VALID scales with hop and elapsed time versus re-derivation): that question presupposes persistence is valuable and is partly subsumed by Graph's freshness work; the discovery question is more foundational because it can invalidate the persistence premise outright; (b) REASSESS C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE: blocked on the unsatisfiable V9_CODE_HASHED_INTO_FREEZE control-plane defect and a three-experiment NO_RECHAIN, so it is not dispatchable; (c) duplicate C-WEB-DYNAMICS: Physics already has the new-observable transaction in flight and Frontier re-scoring the retired estimator family has low marginal value; (d) PARK Frontier: leaves the only idle lane dormant with a well-specified, cheap, decision-changing question available. A cognitive reset (what would Frontier investigate today with no handoff?) lands on the same question, because it tests whether the depth-cost premise that motivates the whole persistence programme is even true.
dependencies: Credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate (already established by EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 and EXP-FRONTIER-37385647440); no cross-lane hard dependency
allocation.question: On the same credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate used by EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378, change the acquisition MECHANISM from same-host link-following BFS to SITE-NATIVE DISCOVERY channels (robots.txt sitemap directives, sitemap.xml, on-site search/query URLs, RSS/Atom feeds, and JSON-LD/structured-data enumeration): over a frozen multi-host pool that is SEPARATELY confirmed to contain DEEP (hop >= 3) state items on at least two distinct hosts/engines, what fraction of those DEEP items can be reached in <= K preregistered GETs (e.g. K=3: one discovery GET plus the item-page GET) using a site-native discovery channel alone, versus only by traversing the hop >= 3 shortest path? Falsifier, arithmetically checkable before freeze and satisfiable in BOTH directions: if the O(1)-reachable fraction of DEEP state items is >= a preregistered materiality threshold (e.g. 0.50) on >= 2 engines, then shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition and persistent path caching is not the optimization target (effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion); if that fraction is below the threshold, then even with site-native discovery fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from a real re-derivation cost. The design must include an attainability certificate that both the DEEP-item admission and the discovery-channel probe are reachable on pinned inputs before freeze, and must disclose per-channel coverage and any channel that yields no admitted DEEP item rather than counting it as a null.
allocation.rationale: Frontier is the only idle lane and its mission is to genuinely leave the current solution basin for high-upside falsifiable mechanisms that could change SPIDER's architecture. Its last bounded result (EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378) validly measured a hop-depth cost-scaling estimator but the DEEP/NEAR ratio was forced by construction, so it could not answer whether depth is a real barrier. The proposed site-native-discovery experiment is materially orthogonal because it changes the acquisition mechanism itself, has a two-sided arithmetically checkable falsifier, and its outcome directly changes a program-level decision: whether persisting traversal paths/procedures is the right memory abstraction, or whether effort should shift to discovery and substrate expansion. It is executable on the already-established credential-free substrate with no cross-lane dependency.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: SPIDER still lacks the integrated causal chain the program audit names as the missing proof: observation -> parameterized mechanism -> executable binding in the shipped kernel -> applicability/freshness decision -> real external agent action -> lower end-to-end cost per successful task. The critical path is unchanged and four of the six lanes are already mid-flight on mandates issued one cycle ago (cycle 37978016186) that remain aligned with the audit: Runtime (EXP-RUNTIME-37973247935, frozen) is closing the last substrate scope bound - whether its composite intervention oracle discriminates changes induced OUTSIDE the surface its author wrote - which gates every downstream real-drift claim; Product (EXP-PRODUCT-37982016598, pre-freeze) is building the credential-free matched-task-family residual-novelty certificate with a CERTIFIED non-ceiling dynamic range, which is the decisive missing quantity for the core thesis 'pay for novelty, not for the whole task'; Intel (EXP-INTEL-37982024058, frozen) is resolving whether any credential-free 3B-8B GGUF clears the minimal Web-agent bar, which determines whether C-LLM-INHERIT is runnable at all; Graph (EXP-GRAPH-37978902447, frozen) is the third bounded attempt at the C-FRESHNESS extraction certificate, now with a pre-freeze satisfiability dry-run; Physics (EXP-PHYSICS-37973239386, frozen) is on a deliberately installed materially new observable (server-minted value predictability) that directly answers its local-attractor flag. Already-frozen transactions are preserved and completed under their frozen design; no new direction should disturb them. The one genuinely idle lane is Frontier: its last bounded result (EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378) measured a hop-depth cost-scaling estimator whose DEEP/NEAR ratio was forced by construction, leaving the deeper and more decision-changing question open - is shortest-path hop a real acquisition-cost barrier at all, or does site-native discovery make deep items reachable in O(1) GETs? That result can change whether persisting paths/procedures is the right optimization target for the whole program. I therefore CONTINUE the four frozen transactions and the Product pre-freeze unchanged, and I reactivate Frontier on the orthogonal acquisition-mechanism question. No lane is left accidentally dormant; no bounded thread is terminated this cycle.
